newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gulf Canada wants UK's Clyde.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gulf Canada wants UK's Clyde.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd joined this year's takeover frenzy sweeping through the oil exploration and production industry by launching a bid on Wednesday for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc.
Gulf Canada said it was making a cash offer of 105 pence per share, valuing Clyde at 432 million pounds ($719.6 million).

The offer, which propelled shares across Britain's oil production sector, comes hot on the heels of the acquisition earlier this month of London-based Santa Fe Exploration by Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA.

"The offer for Clyde follows Gulf Canada's previously stated desire to increase its activities outside of its existing core areas of North America and Indonesia," J. P. Bryan, president and chief executive of Gulf Canada said.
Clyde's North Sea and Australian assets would provide Gulf Canada with additional core areas, and Clyde's Indonesian assets would complement its existing assets, the Canadian firm said.

The company had earlier this year considered a bid for Australia's Command Petroleum Holdings NL, which instead became the takeover target of UK's Cairn Energy Plc. But Gulf Canada said last month Cairn's offer was too high to improve.

The consolidation in the worldwide exploration and production industry started about a year ago and follows half a decade of cost cutting in the oil sector, which has left many firms awash with cash. Gulf Canada, which already owns 1.8 percent of Clyde, said its offer for Clyde represented a premium of 24.3 percent over the mid-market quotation for a Clyde share of 84 1/2 pence at close of trading on December 17.
Clyde' shares had shot ahead 31 pence to stand at 115-1/2 pence in mid-morning trade.
Among other shares in the sector, Cairn Energy, which has promising activities in Bangladesh, jumped 19 pence to 409, while Hardy Oil & Gas Plc climbed 18-1/2 pence to 291-1/2.
Analysts said Gulf Canada's move could be a prelude to more takeover activity in the sector, adding that -- as Clyde shares had risen well above well the bid price -- it could attract a higher offer.
"Clyde is definitely a very attractive company that has been grotesquely undervalued in the market in terms of price to cash flow," said Jurjen Lunshoff, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Gulf Canada plans an offering of its stock and a flotation of its Indonesian unit next year to help fund the proposed acquisition of Clyde.
Bryan said Gulf Canada had arranged a credit line with banks to fund the buy, adding that it had yet to meet with Clyde to discuss the deal.
He told reporters in a conference call that the company wants to raise about $100 million from an offering of its stock in the U.S. and Canada early next year.
Gulf Canada also plans to sell some $300 million in non-strategic assets throughout 1997, assuming its acquisition of Clyde was successful.
In addition, the company is considering to float about 20 percent of its Indonesian unit, Asamera, late next year to raise $300 to $400 million, Bryan said.
